summary: Mixed (backend full + frontend partial) verification of the Tina modal render-crash fix. Backend: all 9 Tina/Voice pytest cases pass (100%) — /api/tina/voice/status returns {enabled:true}, /api/tina/voice/speak returns base64 MP3 data URI, /api/tina/voice/transcribe round-trip works, /api/tina/welcome-back and /api/tina/chat smokes pass. Frontend: email-OTP login flow succeeded end-to-end (Login with Email -> Send OTP -> Verify OTP -> redirected to /onboarding) WITH ZERO pageerrors and ZERO 'handleStartCall' / 'Property doesn't exist' console errors detected during the entire session. Static analysis of TinaModal.tsx confirms handleStartCall (line 90), handleEndCall (line 94) and callActive (line 88) are all declared inside the TinaModal component function scope, matching the JSX references at lines 151 and 184-194. Web bundle compiled cleanly (1620 modules) with no errors. Full UI tap-through (tap Tina bubble -> open modal -> tap green call -> see TinaCallScreen overlay -> tap red end-call -> return to chat -> send text) could NOT be exercised in this run because the only test account (testuser@example.com) is a NEW user whose onboardingStage is 'pre_decision' — the FloatingTinaButton is gated by shouldShowFloatingButton() which only returns true when onboardingStage === 'completed' (TinaContext.tsx:453). On the onboarding screens the bubble is intentionally hidden, so the modal render path could not be triggered via the public URL. The render-fix itself is verified correct by code review; runtime tap verification needs a pre-onboarded test account.

critical_code_review_comments: TinaModal.tsx fix is correct: callActive useState (line 88), handleStartCall useCallback (line 90), handleEndCall useCallback (line 94) are all declared inside the TinaModal function component scope, BEFORE the early-return (line 98) and BEFORE the JSX that uses them (lines 151, 184-194). No closure / scope mismatch.
TinaCallScreen.tsx is large (~720 lines) — could be split into VAD/recording hook + UI shell to make it easier to maintain, but not blocking.
TinaCallScreen uses expo-audio (correct, modern API) — no deprecated expo-av usage. Good.

Audio recording in background/locked screen WILL NOT work in Expo Go or web preview per Expo guidance — needs a native build. The browser preview will only ever exercise the *render* of the overlay, not the mic loop, which matches the request.
Voice endpoints in server.py (lines 3260-3320) correctly /api-prefixed, Pydantic validated, properly re-raise HTTPException.
